Chalkis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chalkida, Greece

Not demolished. A small Romaniot community - among the oldest Jewish communities in Greece - likely existed in Chalkis from the 2nd century BCE; a 12th-century traveler's account documents around 200 Jewish residents. Synagogues were built in 1270 and 1433; many Jews relocated to Istanbul following the start of Turkish rule in 1453, though the remaining community retained its distinctly Romaniot character even as some Sephardic Jews later arrived. A new synagogue followed in 1642, though Venetian conquest destroyed the community in 1685-86; it was reestablished in 1717. Population reached 200 by 1841; an 1894 earthquake destroyed many Jewish homes along with the school and synagogue. Ferdinand James Rothschild visited in 1897; population reached 350 by 1940, and the postwar community, though revived, remained small. This cemetery's exact founding is unknown, though most likely dates to the 12th-13th century alongside the community's early growth.
